# Purpose

This document describes the input structure expected by the `cleaned` model functions. It is intended for developers maintaining the package, app developers connecting iCLEANED to the package, and data engineers building batch-processing or API connectors.

The main input is a nested scenario object, usually named `para`. It can be read from JSON with `jsonlite::fromJSON()` or built by the iCLEANED app.

# Top-Level Input Sections

| Section | Type | Required for | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `livestock` | Data frame | Feed, energy, productivity, GHG, water | Livestock categories, herd structure, animal performance, nutrient requirements, manure management, and IPCC category fields. |
| `seasons` | Data frame | Feed, energy, land | Must include `season_name` and `season_length`. Season lengths are used to split annual requirements. |
| `feed_items` | Data frame, sometimes nested by `crop_name` | Feed, land, soil, nitrogen, water, biomass, GHG | Contains feed nutrient composition and agronomic/spatial parameters. Current functions often call `tidyr::unnest(..., cols = c(crop_name))`, so app/batch builders must preserve that structure where required. |
| `feed_basket` | Data frame/list nested by `feeds` | Feed quality | Describes which feeds are used in each season and their allocation to livestock categories. |
| `fertilizer` | Data frame/list | Nitrogen, GHG | May be empty. If present, fertilizer labels and nitrogen fractions must match expected names. |
| Scalar farm, climate, soil, land-use, manure, and waste fields | Named values | Multiple modules | These include rainfall, evapotranspiration, soil properties, SOC settings, purchased organic inputs, and waste rates. |

# Scalar Fields

These fields are read directly by one or more modules.

| Field | Used by | Expected meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `farm_code`, `farm_name` | Outputs and metadata | Scenario or farm identifiers. |
| `annual_prec` | Soil health, nitrogen, water | Annual precipitation. |
| `rain_length` | Soil health | Length of rainy period used to estimate rainfall erosivity. |
| `et` | Water | Reference evapotranspiration used with crop coefficients. |
| `region` | GHG | Region used for IPCC/manure parameter lookup. |
| `climate_zone`, `climate_zone_2` | GHG | Climate-zone labels used by IPCC parameter tables. |
| `soil_description` | Soil health, nitrogen | Soil class/description label. |
| `soil_k_value` | Soil health | Soil erodibility factor. |
| `soil_n` | Nitrogen | Soil nitrogen concentration or soil N parameter on the package basis. |
| `soil_c` | Nitrogen, SOC | Soil carbon parameter on the package basis. |
| `soil_clay` | Nitrogen | Soil clay percentage used in nitrogen loss equations. |
| `soil_bulk` | Nitrogen, SOC | Soil bulk density. |
| `soil_depth` | SOC | Soil depth used to estimate soil carbon stock. |
| `cropland_system` | SOC | Cropland land-use category; must match stock-change parameter labels. |
| `cropland_tillage` | SOC | Cropland tillage category; must match stock-change parameter labels. |
| `cropland_orgmatter` | SOC | Cropland organic matter/input category. |
| `grassland_management` | SOC | Grassland management category. |
| `grassland_implevel` | SOC | Grassland input/improvement level. |
| `purchased_manure`, `purchased_compost`, `purchased_organic_n`, `purchased_bedding` | Nitrogen, GHG | Purchased organic nitrogen/input terms. |
| `waste_production_milk`, `waste_distribution_milk`, `waste_processing_milk`, `waste_consume_milk` | Outputs | Milk loss/waste rates used in output aggregation. |
| `waste_production_meat`, `waste_distribution_meat`, `waste_processing_meat`, `waste_consume_meat` | Outputs | Meat loss/waste rates used in output aggregation. |

Older example objects may contain legacy aliases such as `txt_annual_prec` or the misspelled `ferlitizer`. App and batch builders should map these into the current names before running the model.

# Livestock Section

`para$livestock` is expected to be a data frame with one row per livestock category. The exact set of fields varies by livestock type, but the following groups are used by the model.

## Identity and category fields

| Field | Used by | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `livetype_code` | Feed allocation, energy, land, GHG | Stable livestock category code. |
| `livetype_desc` | Energy, productivity, outputs | Human-readable livestock category name. |
| `ipcc_ef_category_t1` | GHG | Tier 1 enteric fermentation category. |
| `ipcc_ef_category_t2` | GHG | Tier 2 enteric fermentation/productivity category. |
| `ipcc_meth_man_category` | GHG/manure and productivity grouping | Methane manure-management category. |
| `ipcc_n_exc_category` | GHG | Nitrogen excretion category. |

## Herd and production fields

| Field | Expected basis |
|---|---|
| `herd_composition` | Number of animals in the category. |
| `body_weight`, `adult_weight`, `body_weight_weaning`, `body_weight_year_one` | Weight parameters used by energy equations. |
| `annual_growth`, `lw_gain` | Growth/live-weight-gain terms. |
| `annual_milk` | Annual milk per animal. Dry animals may have `annual_milk = 0`; downstream productivity and Ym logic must handle this intentionally. |
| `annual_wool` | Wool production for sheep where applicable. |
| `birth_interval`, `lactation_length`, `litter_size`, `piglets_relying_on_milk` | Reproduction and lactation terms. |
| `carcass_fraction` | Fraction of live-weight gain converted to carcass/meat output. |
| `milk_product`, `meat_product` | Product indicators used by app/database workflows. |

## Nutrient and energy fields

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `fat_milkcontent`, `protein_milkcontent` | Milk composition, percent. |
| `energy_milkcontent`, `energy_meatcontent`, `protein_meatcontent` | Product energy/protein content. |
| `me_maintenance`, `me_growth`, `me_lactation`, `me_lactmilk`, `me_pregnancy`, `me_grazing` | ME-related fields used by the current schema. |
| `cp_maintenance`, `cp_lys_growth`, `cp_lactation`, `cp_lactmilk`, `cp_lys_pregnancy`, `cp_grazing` | CP/lysine-related fields used by energy/protein requirement equations. |
| `n_content` or `n_manure_content` | Manure nitrogen content. The codebase has been moving toward `n_manure_content`; keep mappings explicit. |

## Time allocation and manure fields

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `time_in_stable`, `time_in_onfarm_grazing`, `time_in_offfarm_grazing`, `time_in_non_roofed_enclosure` | Fractions or proportions of time spent in each management location. |
| `manure_in_field`, `manure_in_stable`, `manure_in_non_roofed_enclosure` | Manure allocation or recovery factors. |
| `manure_onfarm_fraction`, `manure_sales_fraction` | Fractions used to split manure retained on farm and exported/sold. |
| `manureman_stable`, `manureman_yard`, `manureman_onfarm_grazing`, `manureman_offfarm_grazing`, `manureman_non_roofed_enclosure` | Manure-management system labels used by GHG lookups. |
| `distance_to_pasture`, `grazing_displacement`, `work_hour`, `water_requirement` | Activity, work, grazing, and water terms used in selected modules. |

# Feed Items Section

`para$feed_items` is central to the model. It links feed nutrient quality with land, water, soil, nitrogen, fertilizer, residue, and biomass parameters.

## Feed identity and classification

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `feed_item_code` | Stable feed item code. |
| `feed_item_name` | Feed item label used to join with feed basket and land requirements. |
| `feed_type_code`, `feed_type_name` | Feed type classification. |
| `crop_name` | Current functions often unnest by this column. It must exist when running modules that call `unnest(..., cols = c(crop_name))`. |
| `category` | Used to identify grasses, tree crops, tree legumes, and legumes for nitrogen fixation. |
| `source_type` | Expected values include `Main` and `Residue`; used in land requirement equations. |

## Minimum feed nutrient profile

For external feed data connectors such as Feedipedia, SSA feeds databases, USDA profiles, or other feed composition services, the minimum nutrient values required by `feed_quality()` are:

| Field | Expected package format | Conversion guidance |
|---|---|---|
| `dm_content` | Percent of fresh matter | Convert fractions to percent by multiplying by 100. Convert g/kg fresh matter to percent by dividing by 10. |
| `me_content` | Metabolizable energy on the package feed database basis, normally per kg dry matter | Convert external ME units to the same basis before inserting. Do not mix MJ/kg DM, kcal/kg DM, and Mcal/kg DM without conversion. |
| `cp_content` | Percent of dry matter | Convert g/kg DM to percent by dividing by 10. |

The code computes:

```r
me_content_fresh <- dm_content * me_content / 100
cp_content_fresh <- dm_content * cp_content / 100
de_fraction <- me_content * 0.066
```

This means `dm_content`, `me_content`, and `cp_content` must be unit-compatible before model execution.

## Land and production fields

| Field | Used by |
|---|---|
| `dry_yield`, `fresh_yield` | Land requirement and yield calculations. |
| `main_product_removal`, `residue_removal` | Land requirement, nitrogen removal, and residue allocation. |
| `residue_dry_yield`, `residue_fresh_yield`, `residue_dm_content` | Residue feed and land requirement calculations. |
| `water_content`, `harvest_index` | Crop/residue calculations and upstream data preparation. |
| `intercrop`, `intercrop_fraction` | Land requirement adjustment. |
| `cut_carry_fraction` | Feed management metadata. |

## Nitrogen and fertilizer fields

| Field | Used by |
|---|---|
| `main_n`, `residue_n`, `n_content`, `n_fertilizer` | Nitrogen balance and GHG soil/fertilizer calculations. |
| `fraction_as_fertilizer`, `fraction_as_manure` | Manure and fertilizer allocation. |
| `ammonia`, `ammonium_nitrate`, `ammonium_sulfate`, `dap`, `n_solutions`, `npk`, `urea` | Fertilizer application amounts. |
| `residue_burnt` | Burning emissions. |

## Water fields

| Field | Used by |
|---|---|
| `kc_initial`, `kc_midseason`, `kc_late` | Crop coefficient average for water use. |
| `wfp_green`, `wfp_blue`, `wfp_grey` | Water footprint metadata where available. |
| `water_regime`, `ecosystem_type`, `organic_amendment` | Rice methane emissions where rice is in the feed basket. |

## Soil erosion and land-cover fields

| Field | Used by |
|---|---|
| `slope_desc`, `slope_length` | Slope length/steepness conversion in `soil_health()`. |
| `landcover_c_factor`, `slope_p_factor` | RUSLE-style erosion calculation. |
| `land_cover`, `land_cover_desc` | Land-cover metadata and app display. |

## Biomass and tree fields

| Field | Used by |
|---|---|
| `trees_ha_dbh25`, `trees_ha_dbh2550`, `trees_ha_dbh50` | Tree density by diameter class. |
| `increase_dbh25`, `increase_dbh2550`, `increase_dbh50` | Annual diameter increments. |
| `average_dbh25`, `average_dbh2550`, `average_dbh50` | Starting tree diameter classes. |
| `time_horizon` | Biomass calculation period. |
| `trees_ha`, `trees_growth`, `trees_removal`, `trees_dhb` | Legacy or supplementary tree fields. |

# Feed Basket Section

`para$feed_basket` links seasons, feeds, and livestock allocations.

Expected structure:

- A `season_name` column matching `para$seasons$season_name`.
- A nested `feeds` column that can be unnested.
- Each feed entry should contain `feed_item_code`.
- Each feed entry should contain nested livestock allocation data with:
  - `livetype_code`
  - `allocation`

`allocation` is interpreted as a percentage and divided by 100 in `feed_quality()`.

# Fertilizer Section

`para$fertilizer` may be empty. If present, the current nitrogen and GHG logic expects fertilizer descriptions that match these labels:

- `Ammonia`
- `Ammonium nitrate`
- `Ammonium sulfate`
- `DAP`
- `N solutions`
- `NPK`
- `Urea`

Expected fields include:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `fertilizer_code` | Stable fertilizer code. |
| `fertilizer_desc` | Label used for lookup in code. |
| `percentage_n` | Nitrogen content as percent. |
| `fraction` | Legacy or supplementary fraction field. |

# External Parameter Objects

The model also requires parameter lists.

| Object | Source | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `energy_parameters` | `inst/extdata/energy_parameters.json` or app database | `energy_requirement()` |
| `ghg_ipcc_data` | `inst/extdata/ghg_parameters.json` or app database | `ghg_emission()` |
| `stock_change_para` | `inst/extdata/stock_change_parameters.json` or app database | `soil_organic_carbon()` |

The GHG parameter object includes IPCC-style tables such as:

- `Table 10.12`
- `Table 10.13`
- `Table_m`
- `Table 10.16`
- `Table 10.17`
- `Table 10.21`
- `Table 10.22`
- `table_11.1_&_table_11.3`
- `table_2.5`
- `table_5.11`
- `table_5.12`
- `table_5.13`
- `table_5.14`
- `fertilizer_table`

# Controlled Vocabularies

Many fields are selected from app dropdowns or parameter-table labels. Values must match the expected labels exactly, or joins and lookups may return empty results.

Important controlled vocabulary groups include:

- Livestock category names and codes.
- IPCC enteric fermentation and manure categories.
- IPCC nitrogen excretion categories.
- Climate zones and regions.
- Fertilizer descriptions.
- Soil description and soil/land-use categories.
- Cropland system, tillage, and organic matter categories.
- Grassland management and input/improvement level categories.
- Slope descriptions such as `Flat (0-5%)`, `Hilly (5-20%)`, `Steep (20-30%)`, and `Extremely steep (30%+)`.
- Feed source tags such as `OFR`, `OFC`, and `IP` embedded in feed names to identify off-farm roughages, off-farm concentrates, and imported concentrates.

# Guidance for API Connectors

External API connectors should not pass raw external data directly into the model. They should transform values into the iCLEANED schema first.

Minimum requirements for feed composition connectors:

- Resolve the feed item selected by the user.
- Return `dm_content`, `me_content`, and `cp_content`.
- Convert units to the package basis.
- Preserve the app's feed item code/name where possible.
- Keep all non-feed fields already selected by the app unless the connector is explicitly responsible for them.

Spatial/climate connectors should map external data into existing scalar fields and dropdown-compatible categories:

- Climate zone and IPCC climate zone.
- Annual precipitation and rain length.
- Reference evapotranspiration.
- Soil texture/description, soil C, soil N, soil clay, bulk density, depth, and erodibility.
- Elevation and slope can support app-side derivation of `slope_desc` and `slope_length`.
- Crop-yield, harvest-index, residue, and crop coefficient data must be converted to the same units used by `feed_items`.

# Validation Checklist

Before running the model, validate that:

- `livestock`, `seasons`, `feed_items`, and `feed_basket` exist and are non-empty.
- `feed_items` has `crop_name` where modules require unnesting.
- `feed_basket$season_name` values match `seasons$season_name`.
- `feed_basket` allocations have matching `livetype_code` values in `livestock`.
- Feed nutrient values are numeric and unit-compatible.
- Fertilizer descriptions match the expected labels if fertilizer data are present.
- Soil, climate, and land-use category labels match parameter tables.
- Required external parameter objects are loaded from the same version of the parameter database as the app.
